Check a submission's fingerprint and provenance

Source: R/submission.R
check_submission.Rd

Every file from download_answers_button() ends with a fingerprint, a SHA-256 of its identifying content, and a loadedFrom block when the page it came from had been restored from an earlier download. This recomputes the fingerprint from the file's own time, device id, loadedFrom, info fields and answers and says whether it still matches, then reports where the file came from. A file whose name or answers were edited by hand after downloading fails the check. It is not proof of anything: the scheme runs in the browser with no secret, so a reader who studies quiz.js can regenerate a fingerprint. It catches the ordinary case, a copied file with the name changed, and makes a resubmission traceable to the file it grew from.

Usage

check_submission(path)

Arguments

path

Path to a JSON file downloaded via download_answers_button().

Value

Invisibly, a list: time (POSIXct, UTC, or NULL), name, email, device (the per-device id), progress (how far the reader got: sections revealed and questions answered, as a list, or NULL), fingerprint (one of "valid", "invalid", "missing", "unchecked"), loaded_from (the file's provenance block as a list, or NULL), screenshots and recordings (how many answers are pasted images and voice recordings). Also prints a summary.

Details

SHA-256 comes from tools::sha256sum(), available from R 4.5.0; on an older R the fingerprint is reported as "unchecked".

See also

submission_time(), load_tutorial(), extract_submission_media().

Examples

answers <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
writeLines('{"time": "52mz7x0xv", "info": {"name": "Ada"}, "answers": []}', answers)
check_submission(answers)
#> Submitted: 2026-01-15 12:00:00 UTC
#> Name: Ada  Email: (none)
#> Device: (none)
#> Progress: not recorded
#> Media: 0 screenshot(s), 0 recording(s)
#> Fingerprint: missing (downloaded before fingerprints, or stripped)
#> Loaded from: nothing (a fresh run of the tutorial)
